fields.why: Prevalence and medians are compared across 3+ levels of race/ethnicity, income, education, age and county urbanization.
These SPDs have 3+ levels with claims; region and state are geography, and sex is a pair.

The Discussion's rural claims (most rural vs most urban counties, higher frequency and intensity) rest on the stated pairwise-test and nonoverlapping-CI rule, so the rurality entry is per-group vs referent only, not side by side; the flag is right.

brief_issues: Rule 1 could also drop the rurality entry, since the claims contrast only the two extreme levels of a six-level variable shown in full; the brief does not say which governs when the table shows all levels.
